summary: Pirfenidone is an oral antifibrotic pyridone indicated for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Its exact mechanism in IPF is not established. It is titrated over 14 days to a maintenance dose of 801 mg three times daily (2403 mg/day) and is taken with food. Key safety concerns are elevated liver enzymes and drug-induced liver injury (including rare fatal cases) requiring baseline and periodic LFTs; photosensitivity and rash (rarely severe cutaneous reactions such as SJS/TEN/DRESS); and gastrointestinal effects. It is metabolized chiefly by CYP1A2, so strong inhibitors (e.g. fluvoxamine) should be avoided and smoking reduces exposure.

moa: The mechanism of action of pirfenidone in the treatment of IPF has not been established. It exhibits antifibrotic and anti-inflammatory activity, attenuating fibroblast proliferation, TGF-beta-stimulated collagen production and inflammatory mediators in experimental models.

absolute: No labeled absolute contraindications (use per warnings)
relative: Severe hepatic impairment / end-stage liver disease - not recommended
End-stage renal disease on dialysis - not recommended
Concomitant strong CYP1A2 inhibitor (e.g. fluvoxamine, enoxacin)

preg: Data in pregnant women are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk. Pirfenidone was not teratogenic in rats and rabbits at multiples of the maximum recommended human dose. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether pirfenidone is present in human milk; it is excreted in rat milk. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding and the mother's clinical need against potential infant risk.
renal: Monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose modification or discontinuation; pirfenidone is not recommended in patients with end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis.
hepatic: ALT/AST/bilirubin elevations and drug-induced liver injury (including rare fatal cases) can occur. Test liver function before and during treatment and reduce dose, interrupt or discontinue as needed. Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP1A2 inhibitors (fluvoxamine, enoxacin) - markedly increase pirfenidone exposure; avoid/discontinue before starting, or reduce dose if unavoidable
moderate: Moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g. ciprofloxacin) - increase exposure; reduce pirfenidone dose to 1602 mg/day with ciprofloxacin 750 mg BID
CYP1A2 inducers and cigarette smoking - decrease exposure and may reduce efficacy; advise smoking cessation
minor: Other hepatotoxic drugs - additive risk of liver enzyme elevation
interactions.food: Take with food - food reduces Cmax (~49%) and AUC (~16%) and lowers adverse-reaction incidence
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol - potential additive hepatic stress
interactions.diagnostics: Can raise ALT, AST and bilirubin - reflected in routine LFT monitoring

pearls: Metabolized ~70-80% by CYP1A2 - avoid strong inhibitors (fluvoxamine); reduce dose with moderate inhibitors (ciprofloxacin); smoking induces CYP1A2 and lowers exposure
Monitor LFTs at baseline and periodically - drug-induced liver injury, including rare fatal cases, has been reported

missed: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time with food. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose. If more than 14 consecutive days of treatment are missed, re-initiate with the 14-day titration; if fewer than 14 days are missed, resume the previous maintenance dose.
overdose: Clinical experience is limited; multiple doses up to 4005 mg/day were tolerated by healthy volunteers over a 12-day escalation. In suspected overdose, provide supportive care with monitoring of vital signs and clinical status.
